h: Barchu and Nevarech: Blessing over the Torah and Blessing over Food

p: that for the blessing over the Torah
while in Bircas HaMazon they instituted
that the Torah is called the Name of Hashem,
"When I call the Name of Hashem,
the blessing over the Torah before it;
and as is brought in the holy Zohar
that the Holy One, blessed be He,
which is said in the forms
"the God of Avraham," and the like;
"The Torah is written and lies ready,"
to be included in the collective.
this teaches that to each one
the Holy One, blessed be He, gives
That is, for each one individually
to include oneself in the collective.
But in the blessing over the Torah,
which is on the Written Torah,
and one need not include himself.
which indicates the attribute of Malchus,
as is brought in the holy Zohar:
this is the Shabbos of Shabbos eve" —
we call it Torah she'b'al peh" —
for with this he includes himself,
as they said in the Yerushalmi
to this attribute, the attribute of Malchus.
And as is brought in the holy Zohar
"'And I shall be sanctified among the Children of Yisrael' —
'For I am Hashem Who sanctifies you' —
'the whole earth is full of His glory,'
within this glory that is below," and so on.
And in the attribute of Malchus,
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ
"the mouth, we call it Torah she'b'al peh,"
for to each one there is revealed
a radiance from the primordial light
which the Holy One, blessed be He, hid away,
the light, in Torah she'b'al peh,
for those who toil in Torah she'b'al peh
And this is what is brought in the holy Zohar
in the secret of the sign of the covenant,
we call it 'hamevorach,'" and so on.

inlineHeadings.text: The Torah as the Name of Hashem
"Each one in his time": the sustenance of the individual
"Es Hashem hamevorach": blessing drawn to Malchus
"I shall be sanctified": from below to above
The source and the sign of the covenant

paragraphs.text: Berachos 21a — "From where is the blessing over the Torah before it from the Torah? For it says, 'When I call the Name of Hashem, ascribe greatness to our God' (Devarim 32:3)."

rich.text: — "From where is the blessing over the Torah before it from the Torah? For it says, 'When I call the Name of Hashem, ascribe greatness to our God' (Devarim 32:3)."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 60a (Beshalach) — "Rabbi Elazar said: They went out to the wilderness to gaze upon the Holy One, and He removed His glorious radiance from there; they went to look for the Holy One and did not find Him. And we learned that the Holy One is called Torah, and water means only Torah, and Torah is none other than the Holy One, blessed be He."

paragraphs.text: Kesubos 67b — "A certain man came before Rava. He asked: On what do you dine? He said: On fattened chicken and aged wine. He said: Are you not concerned about the burden on the community? He said: Do I eat of theirs? I eat of the Merciful One's, as we learned: 'You give them their food in his time' (Tehillim 145:15) — it does not say 'in their time' but 'in his time': to each one the Holy One gives his sustenance in his time."

paragraphs.text: Yerushalmi, Berachos 7:3 — Shmuel said: I do not exclude myself from the community. Rabbi Avin said: Since he says "hamevorach" (who is blessed), he too does not exclude himself from the community.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 93a (Ra'aya Meheimna) — "'And you shall not profane My holy Name, and I shall be sanctified among the Children of Israel' (Vayikra 22:32): this mitzvah is to sanctify Him every day, to raise His holiness from below to above, just as He is holy above… 'I shall be sanctified among the Children of Israel' — above and below: above in three levels, below in three levels."

paragraphs.text: Zohar II 135b (Terumah) — "'Blessed is Hashem, the Blessed One' — this is the drawing forth of blessings from the source of life, the place from which all watering goes forth; and because it is the source, in the secret of the sign of the covenant, we call it 'the Blessed One' (hamevorach) — the spring of the well; once they reach there, the well is surely filled, and its waters never cease."
